cases.setup: Use a public Python checkout with a typing-aware annotation visitor and the reported nested TypedDict example. Include a comparison expression with an undefined type value.
checks: Record resolved current owners and hashed code anchors for call traversal, typing resolution, and tests.
Record actual diagnostics for metadata strings separately from genuine missing type names.
Leave the checkout unchanged.
Produce the applicability-confirmed output only when current evidence supports it; otherwise record FAIL or UNKNOWN and stop editing.

cases.setup: Bind a checkout with confirmed metadata-as-annotation leakage and supported current factory semantics.
checks: The diff separates TypedDict keys/names and NamedTuple labels from selected type values.
Selected TypeVar constraints and bound values remain annotation traversal.
A present cast first argument receives annotation handling without a string-only restriction.
Typing-aware dispatch and ordinary fallback remain visible in the implementation.
Record invalidated diagnostic and import-usage observations and retain explicit validation.

cases.setup: Use a partition-implemented checkout and its current public annotation-test harness.
checks: Inspect assertions for clean nested TypedDict and NamedTuple metadata.
Inspect assertions for missing names in genuine type positions, including nested string references.
Inspect imported-name-use coverage for NamedTuple, TypeVar, and cast.
Inspect class-nesting coverage with appropriate current version constraints.
Existing adjacent assertions remain present rather than being relaxed to hide failures.

cases.setup: Bind public current argv and instructions for all three validation oracles on the final regression-ready checkout.
checks: Execute bound commands and record their exit status and actual diagnostics or test results.
The punctuation-label reproduction produces no metadata-derived undefined-name diagnostics.
Actual unresolved type references still produce the expected diagnostics.
Imported nested type references do not create false unused-import diagnostics.
Focused and adjacent tests are recorded as PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN with explicit scope.
Ordinary calls and typing-aware identity checks retain their behavior.
Do not claim whole-project or cross-project success from changed-test-only results.
